knowledge:
- key_parameters: dccFiles=Character vector of paths to DCC files ;; pkcFiles=Character vector of paths to PKC files ;; phenoDataFile=Path to the experimental metadata/annotation file ;; analyte=Character string specifying the analyte type, either "RNA" or "protein" ;; useDALogic=Logical flag in shiftCountsOne to shift 0 counts by 1 ;; qcCutoffs=List of thresholds (e.g., percentSaturation, minSegmentReads, percentAligned, minNegativeCount, maxNTCCount, minNuclei, minArea) to flag low-quality ROIs ;; norm_method=Normalization method, such as "quant" (quantile), "neg" (negative control), or "hk" (housekeeping) ;; normData=Name of the normalized assay data element to use during coercion ;; coordinates=Character vector of coordinate column names (e.g., c("x", "y")) to enable spatial plotting in downstream objects
- alternatives: Seurat or SpatialExperiment native normalization: The documentation explicitly warns against using Seurat's or SpatialExperiment's native normalization methods for GeoMx data, recommending GeomxTools::normalize() instead ;; SpatialOmicsOverlay: Mentioned as a specialized package for visualizing ROIs on top of immunofluorescent-guided segmentation images, which is difficult in standard packages
- when_to_use: Use this package at the beginning of a GeoMx DSP transcriptomics or proteomics analysis workflow to load raw data, perform platform-specific quality control, aggregate probes to targets, normalize counts, and prepare the data for downstream single-cell or spatial analysis suites
- pitfalls: Coercing to Seurat or SpatialExperiment before aggregating probe-level data to Target-level data will throw an error ;; Coercing without normalization or without setting forceRaw = TRUE will throw an error ;; Specifying an invalid normData assay name during coercion will throw an error ;; GeoMxSet objects can only read in one analyte at a time; RNA and protein data must be loaded into separate objects by specifying the analyte parameter

workflows.name: rna_preprocessing_and_coercion
workflows.intent: Read, QC, aggregate, normalize, and coerce GeoMx RNA data to Seurat or SpatialExperiment objects.
workflows.stages: 1. Read raw data using readNanoStringGeoMxSet ;; 2. Shift zero counts by one using shiftCountsOne ;; 3. Flag low-quality segments and probes using setSegmentQCFlags and setBioProbeQCFlags ;; 4. Filter out flagged low-quality ROIs and probes ;; 5. Aggregate probe-level counts to target-level counts using aggregateCounts ;; 6. Normalize target counts using normalize ;; 7. Coerce the normalized target-level object to Seurat using as.Seurat or SpatialExperiment using as.SpatialExperiment
workflows.code:
demoData <- suppressWarnings(readNanoStringGeoMxSet(dccFiles = DCCFiles, pkcFiles = PKCFiles, phenoDataFile = SampleAnnotationFile, phenoDataSheet = "CW005", phenoDataDccColName = "Sample_ID", protocolDataColNames = c("aoi", "cell_line", "roi_rep", "pool_rep", "slide_rep")))
demoData <- shiftCountsOne(demoData, useDALogic=TRUE)
demoData <- setSegmentQCFlags(demoData, qcCutoffs = list(percentSaturation = 45))
demoData <- setBioProbeQCFlags(demoData)
lowSaturation <- which(protocolData(demoData)[["QCFlags"]]$LowSaturation)
lowQCprobes <- which(featureData(demoData)[["QCFlags"]]$LowProbeRatio | featureData(demoData)[["QCFlags"]]$GlobalGrubbsOutlier)
passedQC <- demoData[-lowQCprobes, -lowSaturation]
target_demoData <- aggregateCounts(passedQC)
norm_target_demoData <- normalize(target_demoData, norm_method="quant", desiredQuantile = .75, toElt = "q_norm")
demoSeurat <- as.Seurat(x = norm_target_demoData, normData = "q_norm")
demoSPE <- as.SpatialExperiment(norm_target_demoData, normData = "q_norm")

workflows.name: protein_preprocessing
workflows.intent: Read, QC, filter, and normalize GeoMx protein data.
workflows.stages: 1. Read raw protein data using readNanoStringGeoMxSet with analyte = "protein" ;; 2. Flag and remove low-quality ROIs using setSegmentQCFlags ;; 3. Identify and filter low-signal proteins using qcProteinSignal and qcProteinSignalNames ;; 4. Evaluate normalization options using concordance plots with plotConcordance and plotNormFactorConcordance ;; 5. Normalize protein data using normalize
workflows.code:
proteinData <- suppressWarnings(readNanoStringGeoMxSet(dccFiles = DCCFiles, pkcFiles = PKCFiles, phenoDataFile = SampleAnnotationFile, phenoDataSheet = "Annotations", phenoDataDccColName = "Sample_ID", protocolDataColNames = c("Tissue", "Segment_Type", "ROI.Size"), configFile = NULL, analyte = "protein", phenoDataColPrefix = "", experimentDataColNames = NULL))
proteinData <- setSegmentQCFlags(proteinData, qcCutoffs = list(percentSaturation = 45, minSegmentReads=1000, percentAligned=80, minNegativeCount=10, maxNTCCount=60, minNuclei=16000, minArea=20))
lowSaturation <- which(as.data.frame(protocolData(proteinData)[["QCFlags"]])["LowSaturation"] == TRUE)
passedQC <- proteinData[, -lowSaturation]
hk.names <- hkNames(proteinData)
igg.names <- iggNames(proteinData)
fig <- qcProteinSignal(object = proteinData, neg.names = igg.names)
proteinOrder <- qcProteinSignalNames(object = proteinData, neg.names = igg.names)
plotConcordance(object = proteinData, targetList = igg.names, plotFactor = "Tissue")
normfactors <- computeNormalizationFactors(object = proteinData, area = "AOI.Size.um2", nuclei = "Nuclei.Counts")
plotNormFactorConcordance(object = proteinData, plotFactor = "Tissue", normfactors = normfactors)
proteinData <- normalize(proteinData, norm_method="hk", toElt = "hk_norm")
proteinData <- normalize(proteinData, norm_method="neg", toElt = "neg_norm")
proteinData <- normalize(proteinData, norm_method="quant", desiredQuantile = .75, toElt = "q_norm")
